322856.title: Period formula conjecture for subtraction games with FES sets of size 3
322856.statement:
Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers such that $b>3a$ and $\gcd(a,b)=1$. Consider the nim sequence for the finite subtraction set $a,b,a+b$ and let $p$ denote its period.

**Period formula conjecture.** If there exists a multiple $m$ of $2a$ satisfying

$$
b<m<a+b,
$$

then $p=3am$. If no such $m$ exists, then there is some other integer $n$ satisfying

$$
b<n<a+b
$$

such that $p=3an$.

The preceding theorem establishes pure arithmetic periodicity for every subtraction set of size $3$, but the period length is not determined in general. This conjecture proposes a specific form for the period when $b>3a$, after reducing to relatively prime $a$ and $b$ using the scaling behavior of these games.

At a=1 the required open interval (b,b+1) has no integer, while the source table already lists periods/saltus. Literal endpoint correction receives zero credit. Intended corrected all-parameter period formula not resolved.

322882.title: The directed out-star inducibility conjecture
322882.statement:
Let $\vec{S}_k$ be the directed out-star of order $k$, and let $\pi_{\vec{S}_k}(\emptyset)$ denote its inducibility among directed graphs. Define

$$
\alpha_k=\max_{x\in[0,1]}\frac{kx(1-x)^{k-1}}{1-x^k}.
$$

**The directed out-star conjecture.** For every $k\geq3$,

$$
\pi_{\vec{S}_k}(\emptyset)=\alpha_k,
$$

with the unique stable extremal configuration being a blow-up of $\vec{S}_2$ iterated inside part $1$, assigning a proportion $\alpha_k$ of the vertices to part $1$ at every iteration. The claim is known in the source for $k=3$ and $k=4$, but remains conjectural for general $k$.

Stability uniqueness is not independently proved in this lane; no fresh full-scope resolution claimed.

322924.title: The equality of replication numbers for cycles and paths
322924.statement:
Let $P_n$ and $C_n$ denote, respectively, the path and cycle on $n$ vertices, and let $\rho_R(G)$ denote the replication number of a graph $G$. **The cycle–path replication conjecture.** For every $n\geq 6$,

$$
\rho_R(C_n)=\rho_R(P_n).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by computations and an observed relationship between the replication numbers of cycles and paths; its validity for all $n\geq 6$ is left open in the source.

324812.title: Conjecture on sparse graphs with average degree and strong chromatic index of the same order
324812.statement:
Let $d(n)$ be a function tending to infinity. **Average-degree strong-index conjecture.** There exists such a function $d(n)$ that, for every constant $c$, there is a graph on $n$ vertices with average degree $d(n)$ and strong chromatic index at most $cd(n)$.

This asks whether the strong chromatic index can remain linear in the average degree for graphs whose average degree grows with the number of vertices. The source presents it as a conjecture motivated by the possibility that no nontrivial lower bound depending only on average degree exists; no resolution is given in the paper.

324843.title: The second signed path conjecture for pairs of binary trees
324843.statement:
Let $D$ and $R$ be finite, binary trees with the same number of leaves. An edge path in the associahedron from $D$ to $R$ is **sign consistent** when its sign structure is balanced; equivalently, its rotations admit a compatible sign assignment throughout the path.

**Second signed path conjecture.** For every pair $(D,R)$ of finite, binary trees with the same number of leaves, there is a sign consistent path from $D$ to $R$.

The source states that this is equivalent to the first signed path conjecture via the sign-consistency theorem. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

324899.title: Decreasing pattern minimizes avoidance among alternating permutations
324899.statement:
Let $A_n(q)$ denote the set of alternating permutations of length $n$ avoiding the pattern $q$, and let $S_k$ be the symmetric group on $k$ letters. **Alternating-avoidance minimization conjecture.** For all positive integers $k,n$ and all $q\in S_k$ with $q\ne k(k-1)(k-2)\cdots1$,

$$
|A_n(q)|\ge |A_n(k(k-1)(k-2)\cdots1)|.
$$

If $n\ge2k-2$ is even, then the inequality is strict. The claim is motivated by brute-force enumerations, is known for $k=3$, and the case $n=2k-2$ was proved in the cited corollary.

325169.title: The total-order conjecture for trees under the independence-polynomial order
325169.statement:
Let $\succeq$ be the order on graphs defined by comparing their independence polynomials, and let $\mathcal{T}_n$ be the set of trees with $n$ vertices. **Total-order conjecture.** For any two trees $T_1,T_2\in\mathcal{T}_n$,

$$
T_1\succeq T_2\quad\text{or}\quad T_2\succeq T_1.
$$

The claim would make all trees of a fixed order comparable under this graph order. The paper notes that the order is not total on all graphs and gives partial ordering results for trees, but does not prove totality for all trees.

325918.title: Eigenvalue ratio conjecture for nonnegatively curved Alexandrov spaces
325918.statement:
Let $k$ be a natural number, and let $X$ be a compact finite-dimensional Alexandrov space of nonnegative curvature. Write $\lambda_k(X)$ for its $k$-th eigenvalue of the relevant Laplacian.

**Eigenvalue ratio conjecture.** For every natural number $k$, there exists a positive constant $C_k$ depending only on $k$ such that

$$
\lambda_k(X)\leq C_k\lambda_1(X).
$$

This conjecture concerns uniform polynomial-type control of higher eigenvalues by the first eigenvalue on compact nonnegatively curved Alexandrov spaces. The supplied source does not state whether it has been resolved.

326223.title: On-line Ohba conjecture
326223.statement:
For a graph $G$, write $\operatorname{ch}^{\mathrm{OL}}(G)$ for its on-line choice number and $\chi(G)$ for its chromatic number. **On-line Ohba conjecture.** If

$$
|V(G)|\leq 2\chi(G),
$$

then

$$
\operatorname{ch}^{\mathrm{OL}}(G)=\chi(G).
$$

This is presented as a slightly restricted on-line analogue of Ohba's Conjecture. The source gives the equality for the graphs $K_{2*k}$ as evidence, but the asserted statement for all graphs satisfying the order bound remains open.

326269.title: Monotonicity conjecture for induced-subdivision detection
326269.statement:
Let $D$ and $D'$ be digraphs. For a digraph $G$, let $i_D$ (respectively, $i'_D$) denote the corresponding induced-subdivision detection problem. Say that $D$ is an **induced subdigraph** of $D'$ if $D'$ contains a vertex-induced copy of $D$.

**Monotonicity conjecture.** If $i_D$ (respectively, $i'_D$) is NP-complete, then for every digraph $D'$ containing $D$ as an induced subdigraph, $i_{D'}$ (respectively, $i'_{D'}$) is NP-complete.

The conjecture is proposed as a tool for proving a full complexity dichotomy. It covers both variants discussed in the paper and is open according to the surrounding remarks.

326345.title: Extremality of towers of cubes for maximal chains
326345.statement:
Let $X=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, let $\mathcal{P}(X)$ be its power set, and suppose that $n=tk$ with $t,k\in\mathbb{N}$. For $1\leq i\leq k$, set $X_i=\{(i-1)t+1,\dots,it\}$, and define the **tower of $t$-cubes** by

$$
\mathcal{T}_t=\{A:(X_1\cup\dots\cup X_s)\subseteq A\subseteq(X_1\cup\dots\cup X_{s+1})\text{ for some }0\leq s\leq k-1\}.
$$

For $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(X)$, let $c(\mathcal{A})$ denote the number of maximal chains contained in $\mathcal{A}$. **Tower-of-cubes conjecture.** If $|\mathcal{A}|=|\mathcal{T}_t|$, then

$$
c(\mathcal{A})\leq c(\mathcal{T}_t).
$$

The construction is extremal when $t=2$, while the conjecture proposes extremality for every $t$. The cases $t=3$ and $t=n/2$ are highlighted as particularly appealing.

326700.title: Regular-cycle proportion conjecture for primitive permutation groups
326700.statement:
Let $(G,\Omega)$ be a primitive permutation group not covered by the structural conjecture above. For $g\in G$, let $o_g$ denote the number of regular cycles of $g$, and let $c_g$ denote the total number of cycles of $g$, including cycles of length $1$.

\frac{o_g}{c_g}>c.

326856.title: The Nase conjecture on triple cumulative edge bounds in simple graph drawings
326856.statement:
Let $D$ be a simple drawing of a graph, and let $E_{{\le}{\le}{\le}k}(D)$ denote the number of its $\le\!\le\!\le k$-edges, defined by

$$
E_{{\le}{\le}{\le}k}(D)=\sum_{j=0}^{k}E_{{\le}{\le}j}(D)=\sum_{i=0}^{k}{k+2-i\choose 2}E_i(D).
$$

Here $E_i(D)$ denotes the number of $i$-edges, and the cumulative notation is obtained by summing the corresponding lower-order edge counts. **The Nase conjecture.** If $n\ge 3$ and $D$ is a simple drawing of $K_n$, then for every $k$ satisfying $0\le k<n/2-1$,

$$
E_{{\le}{\le}{\le}k}(D)\ge 3{k+4\choose 4}.
$$

The conjecture is stronger than Hill's conjecture. It is implied by the paper's theorem for simple $x$-monotone drawings, and all examples considered by the authors satisfy it; its validity for arbitrary simple drawings remains open.

356170.title: The independent spanning trees conjecture
356170.statement: Let $G$ be a graph and let $v$ be any specified vertex of $G$. A collection of spanning trees of $G$ is **independent spanning trees rooted at $v$** if, for every vertex $u$, the paths from $v$ to $u$ in the trees are pairwise internally vertex-disjoint. A graph is $k$-connected if deleting fewer than $k$ vertices leaves it connected. **Independent spanning trees conjecture.** For any $k \geq 2$, every $k$-connected graph has $k$ independent spanning trees rooted at any vertex. The conjecture is a foundational strengthening of connectivity via spanning-tree packings. It is known for $k \leq 4$ and for planar graphs, but remains open for general $k \geq 5$.

361148.title: Bounded-distance crossings conjecture for quasi-transitive 1-planar graphs
361148.statement:
Let $G$ be a quasi-transitive graph of bounded degree with a plane embedding in which every edge has at most one crossing. For crossing edges $uv$ and $xy$, let $d_G$ denote graph distance.

**Bounded-distance crossings conjecture.** There is an integer $k$ such that for every pair of crossing edges $uv,xy$ in $G$, we have

$$
d_G(u,x)\leq k.
$$

365224.title: Edge bound conjecture for minimally ${\cal R}_d$-connected graphs
365224.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a **minimally ${\cal R}_d$-connected graph**, meaning that $G-e$ is not ${\cal R}_d$-connected for every edge $e\in E(G)$. The graph $K_{d+2}$ denotes the complete graph on $d+2$ vertices.

**Edge-bound conjecture.** One has

$$
|E|\leq (d+1)|V|-\binom{d+2}{2},
$$

with equality if and only if $G=K_{d+2}$.

The cases $d=1,2$ were settled in the cited work of Jear, while the general-dimensional assertion is the subject of the conjecture.

381159.title: Spectral eigenvalue conjecture for the Dirac soliton linearization
381159.statement: Let the spectral problem be the linearized spectral problem denoted by (third), with parameter $\omega\in(-1,1)$. Its isolated eigenvalues and end-point resonances are considered as functions of $\omega$. **Spectral eigenvalue conjecture.** The spectral problem has exactly two isolated eigenvalues and no end-point resonances for all $\omega\in(-1,1)$. The non-zero eigenvalue is positive for all $\omega\in(-1,0)$ and negative for all $\omega\in(0,1)$. This spectral assertion describes the eigenvalue configuration governing the stability analysis of the Dirac solitons. The supplied text does not indicate whether it has been proved or disproved.

381235.title: Eventual odd circular mixing conjecture for bipartite graphs
381235.statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph. A graph is **$(p,q)$-mixing** when it has the circular mixing property with parameters $p$ and $q$.

**Eventual odd circular mixing conjecture.** There exists an integer $q_0$ such that, for every integer $q\geq q_0$, the graph $G$ is $(2q+1,q)$-mixing.

If true, this would show that every bipartite graph has circular mixing threshold at most $2$, addressing the paper's observation that no bipartite graph is currently known with circular mixing threshold greater than $2$.
